title: Partitions with no rows
prompt: What does this program print? Adaptive execution is off, so Spark keeps every partition it makes. `used` counts the partitions that hold at least one row. Three of the 12 lesson trips were driven by `DRV-003`, and none is longer than 100 miles. Type each printed line on its own line.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")


def used(df):
    return df.select(F.spark_partition_id().alias("p")).distinct().count()


two = trips.limit(2).repartition(4)
print(two.rdd.getNumPartitions(), used(two))

one_driver = trips.filter(F.col("driver_id") == "DRV-003").repartition(3, "driver_id")
print(one_driver.rdd.getNumPartitions(), used(one_driver))

none = trips.filter(F.col("trip_distance") > 100)
print(none.repartition(3).rdd.getNumPartitions(), used(none.repartition(3)), none.groupBy("driver_id").count().rdd.getNumPartitions())
hints: A partition can exist and be empty. `getNumPartitions()` counts partitions; `used` counts only those with rows.
Round-robin deals 2 rows to 2 partitions. Hash partitioning puts every row of one key in one partition.
With adaptive execution off, a shuffle always makes the number of partitions asked for (or `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` for a grouping), even when no row reaches them.
explanation: `repartition(4)` always makes 4 partitions, but round-robin deals the 2 rows into only 2 of them. All 3 `DRV-003` trips have the same key, so hash partitioning puts them in one of the 3 partitions. With no rows, `repartition(3)` still makes 3 partitions, all empty, and a grouping still makes the setting's 4. The program turns adaptive execution off first, so no partitions are merged after a shuffle and every count is the one asked for.
